locations.note: D-Day Kick Off, May 1944: weeks before the landings the commandos knock out the coastal batteries at La Rivière on the Normandy coast.
The opening seven missions hit German installations in occupied Norway, 1940-42.
October 1942, on the eve of El Alamein, the commandos blow up a fuel depot at Tell el Eisa and an occupation headquarters at Bab el Qattara.
Operation Icarus, November 1942: with Rommel retreating to El Agheila, the commandos rescue a downed RAF pilot who flies them out.
In the Soup, December 1942: the commandos destroy four German drilling rigs at the Marada oasis.
Up on the Roof, March 1943: the commandos fight their way out of occupied Tunis.
David and Goliath, May 1944: the commandos sink a German battleship in the port of Le Havre.
The 'butcher of Paris' is hunted down in Compiègne in August 1944.
In September 1944 the commandos kill German sappers and disarm their charges at Liège; in December, as the Ardennes offensive breaks through, they come back to blow up a bridge.
Before Dawn, November 1944: the commandos free the Resistance leader Claude Gilbert and his men from execution in Ribeauvillé, north of Colmar.
A V2 launch site at Oldenburg, west of Bremen, must be destroyed in January 1945.
The finale, Operation Valhalla, storms a castle at Gundelfingen near Freiburg in February 1945.

routes.name: The Commandos
routes.note: The commandos raid occupied Norway, follow the desert war from El Alamein to El Agheila, Marada and Tunis, sink a battleship at Le Havre and open the way for D-Day, hunt the butcher of Paris at Compiègne, fight at Liège and Ribeauvillé, and push into Germany to wreck a V2 base at Oldenburg and storm a castle at Gundelfingen.
